question.text: Let $p, q$ and $r$ be the sides opposite to the angles $P, Q$ and $R,$ respectively in a $\Delta P Q R .$ If $r^{2} \sin P \sin Q=p q,$ then the triangle is

solution.text:
We know that in $\Delta A B C$ $\frac{a}{\sin A}=\frac{b}{\sin B}=\frac{c}{\sin C}=2 R$
$\therefore \quad r^{2} \sin P \sin Q=p q$
$\Rightarrow r^{2} \cdot \frac{p}{2 R_{1}} \cdot \frac{q}{2 R_{1}}=p q,$ where $R_{1}$ is circumras
of $\Delta P Q R$. $\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & r^{2}=4 R_{1}^{2} \\ \Rightarrow & r=2 R_{1} \\ \Rightarrow & 2 R_{1} \sin R=2 R_{1}\end{array}$
$\Rightarrow \quad R_{1}=90^{\circ}$
$\therefore \Delta P Q R$ is right angled.
